## Calling a subprogram

The Main controls the start of a conveyor; the "Counting" ladder (a `CTU` with a preset of 3 and its indicator) exists but no block calls it.

| Variable | Role | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start`, `stop` | start and stop the conveyor | push buttons (true while pressed) |
| `part_sensor` | detects each part | sensor |
| `clear` | resets the count to zero | push button |
| `conveyor` | conveyor motor | output |
| `batch_indicator` | on when 3 parts are counted | output |

### Task

1. Read the "Counting" ladder, run the analysis (warning: ladder never called) then the simulation: `batch_indicator` does not light up.
2. In the Main, add a network and drag "Counting" into it from the "Programs" section of the explorer. Connect the call block to the rail, without any condition.
3. Check: after three passes of `part_sensor`, `batch_indicator` lights up; `clear` makes it drop.
4. Experiment: place a NO contact on `conveyor` in front of the call block. With the conveyor stopped, leave `part_sensor` true and then start the conveyor: `cpt` counts a part that was never counted. Explain why.

texts.countPartsDescription: The CTU counts the rising edges of part_sensor, reset by clear.
texts.batchIndicatorDescription: On when the batch is complete.
texts.callCountingDescription: Unconditional call: the subprogram runs on every cycle.
